title: Respirometers
examples: How does a respirometer actually measure the rate of respiration?
What does a high respiratory quotient value suggest about the fuel source?
Can we use this method to compare the respiration of different tissues?

explain.say: A respirometer measures the rate of gas exchange in a living organism.
It works by measuring the volume of oxygen consumed or carbon dioxide produced.
The rate of oxygen uptake tells us how fast the organism is respiring.
The respiratory quotient is the ratio of carbon dioxide produced to oxygen consumed.
If the respiratory quotient is one, the fuel source is likely a carbohydrate.
In a real life example, we can use this to compare the energy needs of different muscles.

faq.q: What is the difference between oxygen uptake and carbon dioxide production?
faq.a: Oxygen uptake measures the oxygen taken in during respiration. Carbon dioxide production measures the waste gas released.
asks: How do I measure gas exchange?
Is O₂ uptake the same as CO₂ production?

faq.q: What does a respiratory quotient of zero suggest?
faq.a: A respiratory quotient of zero suggests that no carbon dioxide is being produced, which is unusual for respiration.
asks: What does a very low RQ mean?

faq.q: Does the respirometer measure the total energy released?
faq.a: No, it measures the rate of gas exchange, which is related to, but not the same as, total energy released.
asks: What is the unit for respiration rate?

faq.q: If the RQ is less than one, what is the fuel source?
faq.a: An RQ less than one suggests that the primary fuel source being respired is fats or lipids.
asks: What fuel gives an RQ below one?
Does the fuel type affect the RQ?

faq.q: Can we use this to study living cells in a lab?
faq.a: Yes, respirometers can be adapted to measure gas exchange in isolated tissues or cell cultures under controlled conditions.
asks: Can I test cells with this?
What biological samples can be tested?

facts: Respiration involves the exchange of gases: oxygen in and carbon dioxide out.
The respiratory quotient is calculated by dividing the volume of carbon dioxide by the volume of oxygen.
A carbohydrate fuel source typically yields a respiratory quotient close to one.
Fats generally result in a respiratory quotient value that is less than one.

quiz.say: A student measures the volume of carbon dioxide produced as 10 liters and the oxygen consumed as 10 liters. What is the respiratory quotient?
quiz.why: The respiratory quotient is the ratio of CO₂ produced to O₂ consumed, so 10 divided by 10 equals 1.0.

wrong.1: This incorrectly multiplies the two volumes together.
wrong.2: This incorrectly divides the oxygen volume by the carbon dioxide volume.
wrong.3: This incorrectly adds the two volumes together.

quiz.say: If the respiratory quotient is calculated to be 0.7, what is the most likely fuel source being respired?
quiz.why: An RQ value less than one indicates that the fuel source has a higher proportion of fats.

wrong.0: Proteins generally yield an RQ value that is close to one as well.
wrong.1: Glucose is a type of carbohydrate and should give an RQ of one.
wrong.3: Carbohydrates always result in an RQ value very close to one.

quiz.say: A student measures 50 milliliters of oxygen used and 25 milliliters of carbon dioxide produced. What is the respiratory quotient?
quiz.why: The ratio is carbon dioxide divided by oxygen, so 25 divided by 50 equals 0.5.

wrong.1: This incorrectly calculates the ratio of oxygen to carbon dioxide.
wrong.2: This incorrectly adds the two volumes together.
wrong.3: This incorrectly uses the volume of oxygen consumed as the answer.
